human_tolerance.notes: Authored representation: the national-scale activity series does not support an urban-affinity estimate.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: ADW describes breeding in spring and early summer. Dates map those seasons to southern-hemisphere months; they are an approximate seasonal window, not a study-specific calendar.

vocalizations.description: A clucking contact call used between kangaroos.
A guttural cough given by alarmed kangaroos and aggressive males.

taxonomy.note: GBIF match returned canonical Macropus giganteus, SPECIES, ACCEPTED; provider record confirms the classification.

external.note: Checked provider records 2026-11-01. GBIF usageKey 5219981 is accepted species Macropus giganteus; iNaturalist taxon 42888 is active, species rank, Macropus giganteus.

conservation.note: Account lists Least Concern; maintained here as an openly attributed, last-resort NC fact.

range.note: ADW describes the native range along eastern Australia, including Queensland, New South Wales and Tasmania; coded at country scale as AU. No introduced-country claim is made.

traits.limb_count.note: Four limbs; the long tail is not a limb.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Hopping is stated as the characteristic locomotion.

traits.nest_type.note: Marsupial; no nest structure is described.

traits.perching.note: Ground-dwelling macropod; perching is not reported.

traits.size_class.note: Large follows the sourced adult mass range and body length.

traits.mass_kg.note: The account says females usually weigh up to about 40 kg and males can reach 90 kg. 40 kg is used as a sourced representative adult anchor; this compresses strong sexual dimorphism and is not a population mean.

traits.length_m.note: ADW reports a 1.5–1.8 m range; 1.5 m is the sourced lower adult length used as a conservative representative.

traits.lifespan_y.note: Life/Longevity narrative says 7–10 years in wild and its structured field gives Average lifespan, wild: 8 years. The separate captive 25-year high, captive typical 18–20, and Max Planck rows of 19.8–20 years are excluded because they do not establish typical wild lifespan.

traits.diet.note: Grazing herbivore; grass is described as the main food.

traits.senses.note: Authored generic mammalian sensory values; no species-specific evidence used.

traits.social.note: ADW describes mobs but gives varying group composition; [10,20] is an authored coarse size range, anchored to its small-group account and Australian Museum report of mobs of 10 or more.

traits.activity_pattern.note: ADW says animals rest in shade most of the day and feed from dusk until dawn.

traits.defense.note: Flee is inferred from hopping mobility and alarm foot-stamping, with no claim of fighting as routine defense.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement for a large wild herbivore that rests under cover and stamps when alarmed.

habitat.use.note: Ground use is authored from terrestrial grassland/woodland habitat descriptions; proportions are judgement.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Account reports resting in shade under trees or scrub; mapped to generic shelter.

habitat.resources.note: Grass grazing is directly supported; shelter and water resource weights are simulation mappings, not measured diet proportions.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Authored conservative simulation estimate; national activity data does not resolve urban tolerance.

seasonal.strategy.note: ActiveYearRound is an authored broad strategy; continuous breeding is reported, while no migration or dormancy claim is made.

seasonal.phases.note: ADW states spring and early summer; mapped to southern-hemisphere September through January. This month window is a season conversion, not a measured population-specific calendar.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Juvenile and adult labels only; age and scale values are omitted.

behavior.note: Species-local FSM maps reported hopping, grazing, shade-resting and dusk-to-dawn feeding to available actions. It approximates time of day with solar elevation, not a strict clock interval.

vocalizations.note: ADW reports clucking contact calls and guttural alarm coughs; time windows are broad because exact schedules are not stated.

look.note: Judgement based on sourced powerful hind legs, long balancing tail, grey fur, darker face and tail tip. Proportions, pose and palette are authored block-model approximations.
